quiz.0.question: During the Appassimento drying process, approximately how much weight do the grapes lose?
quiz.0.explanation: Grapes for Amarone are dried on bamboo mats (arele) for 90–120 days, losing approximately 30–40% of their weight through dehydration — concentrating sugars, acids and flavour compounds.
quiz.1.question: In Amarone's ageing evolution, which phase is considered the 'first peak of drinkability'?
quiz.1.explanation: Most serious Amarone reaches its first major peak around 7–12 years from the harvest — the tannins have softened, the fruit has integrated with secondary complexity, and the wine shows its first hints of evolved character.
quiz.2.question: Which description most accurately describes top producer styles?
quiz.2.options.0: All top producers use the same style
quiz.2.options.1: Dal Forno Romano produces the most concentrated, extracted style; Quintarelli is the classic, contemplative traditionalist; Allegrini is the modern benchmark
quiz.2.options.2: Traditional producers are better than modern producers
quiz.2.options.3: Small producers always make better Amarone than large ones
quiz.2.explanation: Dal Forno Romano: most concentrated and opulent (longest drying). Quintarelli: the gold standard of classical Amarone — complex, meticulous, multi-year ageing. Allegrini: modern precision and consistency.
quiz.3.question: Which of the following is the most fatal error in long-term Amarone storage?
quiz.3.options.1: Temperature fluctuation — cycling between hot and cold repeatedly
quiz.3.explanation: Temperature fluctuation is the most destructive factor for wine storage. For a concentrated, long-lived wine like Amarone, repeated temperature swings cause expansion/contraction of the cork and premature oxidation.
